lecture_09.title: CS336 Spring 2026, Lecture 9: Scaling laws - basics
lecture_09.anchor_convention: lecture_09.pdf:p<page>, page numbers from `pdftotext -layout` form feeds (title slide = p1; 57 content pages, p58 empty)
lecture_09.note: Evidence is the text layer of the slides (lecture_09.txt), split page-by-page by discover_slides.py into discovered.json. Most plots (Kaplan's three L(N)/L(D)/L(C) fits, the Hestness exponent table, the critical-batch S/E curve, the Chinchilla IsoFLOP parabolas and its a/b exponents, the data-repetition formula) are screenshots whose numbers are not in the text layer; each KP's filtering_note says when a number is figure-only. Stacked fractions and bracketed expressions on p17, p19 and p43 are mangled by layout extraction (listed under `dropped` in discovered.json); the reconstructed form is stated in the KP with the mangled text quoted verbatim.

lecture_02.title: CS336 Spring 2026, Lecture 2: Resource accounting
lecture_02.note: Referenced only through external_prerequisites (lecture_02:six-nd, lecture_02:napkin-training-time); see atlas/lectures/lecture_02/knowledge_points.json. Supplies C = 6ND, which the deck assumes when it writes N_opt and D_opt as functions of C.

kaplan_2020.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models (Kaplan, McCandlish, Henighan, Brown, et al., 2020)
kaplan_2020.note: Cited on p13, p15, p30 ('Kaplan+ 2021' on p30 is the same paper), p43, p45, p50. The deck prints only the compute-optimal exponents N_opt = C^0.73, D_opt = C^0.27 (p45/p50); the L(N), L(D), L(C) power-law exponents and the L(N,D) bracket form are shown as figure screenshots.

hoffmann_2022.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Hoffmann et al., 2022; 'Chinchilla')
hoffmann_2022.note: Spelled 'Hoffman' on p45. Source of the three fitting methods (p46-p49) and the 20 tokens/parameter figure (p54). Chinchilla's own fitted exponents (a, b near 0.5) are not in the deck's text layer, but p46's image prints the paper's Table 2 (0.50/0.50, 0.49/0.51, 0.46/0.54; Kaplan 0.73/0.27) and p47-p49 print the Gopher-budget projections (67B/1.5T, 63B/1.4T, 40B).

hestness_2017.title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically (Hestness et al., 2017)
hestness_2017.note: p10-p11 (earliest large-scale neural scaling study; MT, LM, speech; 'emergence', compute scaling), p14 (logistic-like curve shape), p18 (measured exponents, printed on the figure: MT −0.13, speech −0.30), p32 (Adam vs SGD on RHNs).

banko_brill_2001.title: Scaling to Very Very Large Corpora for Natural Language Disambiguation (Banko & Brill, 2001)
banko_brill_2001.note: p8: log-linear scaling with data; figure only.

kolachina_2012.title: Prediction of Learning Curves in Machine Translation (Kolachina et al., 2012)
kolachina_2012.note: p9: early test of functional forms; power-law relation between data and downstream (BLEU) performance.

bahri_2021.title: Explaining Neural Scaling Laws (Bahri, Dyer, Kaplan, Lee, Sharma, 2021)
bahri_2021.note: p20: intrinsic-dimensionality account of the exponent alpha; the deck calls the argument 'not airtight'.

hashimoto_2021.title: Model Performance Scaling with Multiple Data Sources (Hashimoto, 2021)
hashimoto_2021.note: p22: data composition shifts the offset, not the slope (figure attribution '[Hashimoto 2021]').

muennighoff_2023.title: Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models (Muennighoff et al., 2023)
muennighoff_2023.note: p24 shows the effective-data formula with the legend D' / U_D / R_D / R_D* but names no author in the text layer; the attribution to this paper is the atlas author's identification of the notation (inference).

rosenfeld_2020.title: A Constructive Prediction of the Generalization Error Across Scales (Rosenfeld, Rosenfeld, Belinkov, Shavit, 2020)
rosenfeld_2020.note: p43-p44: joint data-model law Error = n^-alpha + m^-beta + C; fit on small models and small data, predict the rest.

tay_2022.title: Scaling Laws vs Model Architectures: How does Inductive Bias Influence Scaling? (Tay et al., 2022)

tay_2023.title: Scale Efficiently: Insights from Pre-training and Fine-tuning Transformers (Tay et al., 2023)
tay_2023.note: p41: downstream scaling can be much less predictable than upstream loss. Cited as 'Tay et al 2023' on the slide.

yang_2022.title: Tensor Programs V: Tuning Large Neural Networks via Zero-Shot Hyperparameter Transfer (Yang et al., 2022; muP / muTransfer)
yang_2022.note: p40: optimal learning rate drifts with width under standard parametrization; muP makes it transferable.

yao_2024.title: Yao et al 2024 (cited on p40 next to Yang et al 2022 for scale-aware learning-rate choices)
yao_2024.note: Only the author-year string appears in the text layer; the deck gives no title or link, so the exact paper is not identified here.

besiroglu_2024.title: Chinchilla Scaling: A Replication Attempt (Besiroglu, Erdil, Barnett, You, 2024)
besiroglu_2024.note: p53: data forensics on Chinchilla's Figure 4; re-fitting method 3 brings it in line with methods 1 and 2.

mccandlish_2018.title: An Empirical Model of Large-Batch Training (McCandlish, Kaplan, Amodei, OpenAI, 2018)
mccandlish_2018.note: p38's 'ratio of the trace of the gradient covariance and squared norm of the gradient' is this paper's gradient noise scale; the deck does not name the paper in its text layer (atlas author's identification).

gulrajani_2023.title: Likelihood-Based Diffusion Language Models (Gulrajani & Hashimoto, 2023)
gulrajani_2023.note: p55: IsoFLOP analysis applied to diffusion LMs.

abnar_2025.title: Parameters vs FLOPs: Scaling Laws for Optimal Sparsity for Mixture-of-Experts Language Models (Abnar et al., 2025)
abnar_2025.note: p55: IsoFLOP analysis applied to MoEs; p35-p36 mention MoE scaling laws without a citation in the text layer.

cmu_vc_slides.title: CMU 10-701 lecture 16: VC dimension (Eric Xing)
cmu_vc_slides.note: p6: classical sample-complexity bounds for finite hypothesis classes; context for 'these are upper bounds, not realized loss values'.
